payload.headline: Agent created its own overdue invoice instead of finding an existing one; 4/5 checks failed.
what_went_wrong: Agent assumed sandbox had no invoices and created a new order/invoice instead of properly querying existing overdue invoices with required date params (invoiceDateFrom/To).
The initial GET /invoice call failed with 422 (missing date params), but agent never retried with proper date range — it just fabricated the overdue invoice scenario.
Voucher posting failed first attempt (missing customer field on account 1500 posting), wasting one API call before correcting.
Scoring shows only 1/5 checks passed — likely the partial payment or voucher accounts were wrong, or the 'overdue invoice' found/used was not the pre-existing one the task expected.
what_worked: Voucher was eventually created with correct debit/credit accounts (1500/3400) after fixing the customer field.
Reminder fee invoice was created and sent successfully via PUT /invoice/:send.
what_to_try_next: Always retry GET /invoice with a wide date range (e.g., invoiceDateFrom=2020-01-01&invoiceDateTo=2026-12-31) when the first call fails validation — never assume sandbox is empty.
Before creating any entities, exhaustively search for existing invoices, customers, and orders; the task says 'find the overdue invoice' implying it pre-exists.
Verify the payment registration call includes correct paymentTypeId and amount=5000 explicitly, and confirm the voucher debit/credit sign convention matches what scoring expects.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account — fetching all accounts was broad; could query specific account numbers directly.
POST /order (first one, creating fake overdue invoice) — unnecessary since a real overdue invoice should have been found via proper GET /invoice with date params.
PUT /ledger/account/$REF:account_1920 — setting up bank account may not have been needed if existing account was already configured.
